Retain the selected job ID and local output
path in the scene record rather than duplicating the full provider response.

Sana Sprint is a text-to-image draft model, not an identity-locking image editor.
Do not invent reference-image parameters. Where exact likeness/product identity
is essential, reuse the user's supplied stills or choose a reference-capable
model instead. For recurring characters, draw frames with a `cast.models`
recommended image model (normally `nano-banana-2.1`) and approved `cast` IDs.
For recurring products/sets, retain their
[reference images](film/look-dev.md#reference-images) as additional inputs.
Do not drop `cast` to run a text-only draft model.
With a reference-capable model, the board's style still wins over a supplied
photo: pass the photo for identity only, as
[the style key rule](prompting.md#the-style-key-wins-over-photo-references) says.

If Sana Sprint is unavailable, use `fal-ai/flux/schnell` as the inexpensive
fallback after inspecting its schema. Do not silently switch to a premium model.

Honor requested script, storyboard and first-look checkpoints. An animatic or
previs first look is timed and playable, not a static storyboard. Written content
or storyboard approval shows the full content in the reply immediately before
the question, or in the question itself; write nothing after the question.

## Build the review artifact

Save `storyboard/storyboard.html`, `storyboard/storyboard.json`, and local
images under the active workspace folder. A [board that tells a story](#when-the-board-tells-a-story) opens with its logline
above the cards. Each scene card should contain:

- Stable scene ID, short title, and estimated screen time.
- Its actual generated/supplied still, displayed at the intended aspect ratio.
- What happens and why that beat belongs in the story (in a story, its BUT or
  THEREFORE).
- Framing plus intended subject/camera motion for image-to-video.
- Proposed narration, sound, or exact overlay text when relevant.

For boards that will be animated, use the version-1 shape in [scene records](plan.md),
keeping selected stills in each scene's `image` field.
The JSON records the brief, the logline of a story, shared style, ordered scene IDs, durations, selected
image paths, image prompts/model/job IDs, and proposed motion prompts. Keep image
prompts (one frozen composition) separate from motion prompts (what moves over
time).

Use readable, responsive HTML with inline/local CSS and relative image paths such
as `assets/S01.jpg`. No CDNs, remote image URLs, external fonts, or filesystem
fetch calls: the preview blocks external access and only serves the HTML's folder
and descendants. Put labels/lettering in HTML, not generated pixels.

Link it in the final response using its absolute local path:
`[Storyboard](</absolute/project/storyboard/storyboard.html>)`. Use
`voyager files present ... --title "Storyboard" --deliverable none --json` if the
live CLI accepts HTML (`none`: a storyboard is not a version of the piece);
otherwise the absolute Markdown link is the presentation route.

A storyboard-only request stops here: no video, music, voice, or assembly jobs are
needed to deliver the board.

## Turn the board into video

When the user asks to proceed, read the saved board, group a hand-drawn board's
panels into takes by their joins ([multi-shot practice](continuity.md#multi-shot-practice)), then
generate each take from its references, its panels' framing, staging and action
written into the prompt ([generate shots from references](../SKILL.md#generate-shots-from-references)).
The hand-drawn panels plan the shots; they stay out of the generation inputs.

A frame-accurate board's approved frames are keyframes. Inspect their returned
likeness results (or compare with the hero when the check is unavailable) before
paying for motion, then animate each take with image-to-video and the same `cast` IDs, a segment
between each pair of consecutive approved frames (`image_url`, `end_image_url`),
so every approved frame stays a keyframe, and carry motion across each
CONTINUE join ([carry motion](continuity.md#carry-motion-not-just-a-frame)); report drift or uncertainty honestly.

After collecting the clips, follow [assembly](assembly.md).

## Still approval

For [still review](stills.md), the following is
an example workflow, when review would help.
A storyboard's cheaper draft images are only for a storyboard-only request;
stills to animate are keyframes.

**Estimate.** Estimate the cost of every paid call the approval covers, music, voice
and lip-sync included, with `voyager models estimate` (see
[paid generation](craft/paid-generation.md)), and record the stills in the
[scene records](plan.md). `eleven-music` bills $0.60 per started minute, so a generated
music bed adds at least $0.60; the final cost line totals every job and names the key each
was billed to (FAL, ElevenLabs).

**Ask.** Ask for approval with the host's question tool.
**Put the stills in the question text**: the card shows the stills the question names, so
name every still it asks about, never one the user has not seen.
Start with one plain sentence. Then, for each shot, add a line saying what it shows
and how it will move, followed by the still on its own line as Markdown with its
real absolute path in angle brackets, so paths with spaces work:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```md
Approve these 2 stills for animation?

**S01 · Seed in the soil** (5 s): the seed cracks open and a root pushes down.

![S01](</absolute/project/stills/S01.png>)

S01 → S02: CONTINUE, the root keeps pushing down into the dark soil

**S02 · Root in the dark** (5 s): the root branches as the camera follows it down.

![S02](</absolute/project/stills/S02.png>)
```

Between each pair of shots, write its join on its own line: `S01 → S02: CONTINUE, <what
carries on>` or `S01 → S02: CUT, <the reason the next shot answers>`
([continuity](continuity.md#every-join-is-cut-or-continue)), naming each still as its alt
text or file name does. In-app on Claude and OpenCode, Voyager refuses the question while a
join is unmarked, and once when every join is CUT on a short action: every shot gives its
length as `(N s)` and they total 15 s or less, or Voyager judged the brief one continuous take.

When the piece has speech, add the full script after the stills as a quoted block.

Use one question whose header and text both say "Approve", with these options,
none marked "(Recommended)", so the question waits for the user instead of being
answered automatically:

- "Approve and animate (about $X in all, about N min)"
- "Change the overall direction (Type below)", described as "Type the new
  direction. The stills are redrawn to it, then you see them again."

The text the user types with an option is the change: act on it, and never
follow the answer with a second question asking what is wrong.

Voyager lets the user flag stills to redo, each with an optional note. Then the
answer is a review, perhaps with a `Note:` paragraph after it:

```text
Still review:
- S02: redo — make the hand natural
- S07: redo (fresh take)
(others approved)
```

Without a question tool, send the same text as a message, and ask the user to
name any shots to redo and what to change.

**Revise.** When the user asks for revisions, change only the named stills, and
keep a ledger of their notes from the first redo ([iterate on a take](iterate.md)).
How depends on the flaw:

- A local flaw, confined to one area of an otherwise approved still (a wrong
  hand, a stray object, a logo, a smudge): edit that still with
  [make-image](../../make-image/SKILL.md#generate-or-edit), the still as the image
  to edit and a prompt that changes only that element and keeps everything
  else. When nothing else changed, the still keeps its approval and is not
  asked about again; show it in your reply. When the edit moved more than
  that element, treat it as a replaced still.
- A composition, pose or style flaw: regenerate the still.

For a still review:

- **redo with a note:** change the still as the note says, by the rule above.
- **redo (fresh take):** generate a new take of that shot.
- Every still not listed is approved. Animate those now, at the estimate
  scaled to those shots, and say so.

If another review would help, show only the replaced stills.

A produced film's keyframes follow [generation](film/staged-production.md#generation)
too: each is drawn from its own shot's frame and references rather than chained
from the shot before across a cut, so a revised keyframe changes only its own shot, and each
shot's cost is recorded in `film/GENERATION.md`.

# Restyle existing footage (style transfer)

Use when the user supplies a video (live action, a Blender render, a screen
recording) plus a look (a style image, a game or film still, a written style) and
wants the same video in that look: the same camera, timing, blocking and
composition, with new materials, rendering and styling.

## Give each input one job

The source video supplies motion: camera travel, action timing, silhouettes and
the ending composition. A **restyled anchor frame** supplies the finished
appearance. The user's style reference is what you use to make that anchor; it
is not the anchor itself.

Never make the raw style reference the only appearance input. Expect it to copy that
image's subject, costume or layout, or to apply a light pass that keeps the
source's look almost unchanged.

## Workflow

1. **Choose a video-conditioned endpoint.** Pick one that takes the source
   video, not image-to-video plus a motion prompt; that is a different workflow,
   so don't substitute it silently. Check each candidate's current
   `voyager models show ENDPOINT --json` before the first take:
   - **Seedance 2.5 reference-to-video**
     (`bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-video`) with `task: "editing"`: the
     source in `video_urls`, the anchor in `image_urls`. Check its prompt labels
     and limits in `voyager models show`. Reference video duration affects the
     bill.
   - **LTX render-to-real** (`fal-ai/ltx-2.3-quality/render-to-real`) only when
     the target look is photoreal. It pushes a render toward photorealism, and
     its stronger intensity modes mean more photoreal, so it fights an anime or
     painterly look. The source in `video_url`, the anchor in `image_url` as the
     first frame, a prompt that starts with `3DREAL.`, and an intensity mode.
     Length is capped at about 6 s at 720p and about 15 s at 480p. Output is
     smaller than fal's page says: a 1280×720 source at `720p` came back
     1152×704, and 2048×1152 with `enable_detail_refine` (not 2560×1440; checked
     2026-10-07). Quote those sizes. See the worked
     request in
     [room-to-video's examples](../../room-to-video/references/commands-and-examples.md#generate-a-restyled-finish).
   - **H3 Max 3D to video** (`minimax/h3-max/3d-to-video`) for a Blender or 3D
     source with a photoreal target: the source in `video_url` (up to 15 s and 32
     shots; the output keeps its duration), the anchor and any other appearance
     references in `reference_image_urls` (up to 8). Without references it
     generates its own, so the approved anchor would not be used.
   - **Kling O3 edit** (`fal-ai/kling-video/o3/pro/video-to-video/edit`) when the
     source's sound must be retained: the source in `video_url`, the anchor in
     `image_urls` (prompted as `@Image1`), `keep_audio: true`. With a video, images
     and elements together are capped at 4.

   Use [choose-media-model](../../choose-media-model/SKILL.md) for a comparison.

2. **Fit the source to the endpoint.** Trim and scale a separately named
   derivative to the model's duration, size and fps limits, as in
   [acquire a video reference](acquire-reference.md#supply-it-to-a-generation-model).
   A first-frame endpoint such as LTX render-to-real needs each
   section to open on a representative frame: if it opens on a dissolve or black,
   trim it and record the trim.
3. **Pick each section's anchor frame.** Usually its first frame. Extract it
   with `ffmpeg -ss T -i FILE -frames:v 1 out.png`; pass on `anchor-frame/frame-1.jpg`,
   a still at the source resolution. For a Blender source, render that frame as a
   PNG instead when full resolution matters. Seedance, H3 and Kling treat the
   image as an appearance reference, so any representative frame works there.
4. **Restyle one frame of the actual source, then approve.** Use
   [make-image](../../make-image/SKILL.md) editing with the extracted frame first
   and the style reference second. Prompt for the look (palette, line, shading,
   texture, rendering) and preserve the frame's silhouettes, poses, horizon,
   perspective and object positions. Say that the style reference's subject,
   costume and composition must not carry over unless the user asked for them.
   Use the same style wording for every section's anchor. Compare each anchor
   with its source frame (side by side or overlaid): a shifted pose or prop
   drifts through the whole take, so fix it here. For an unproven multi-section
   setup, a priced first-section pilot may help the user judge the result.
5. **Submit each section with its approved anchor.** Condition the chosen
   endpoint on the fitted source and its approved anchor, never on the raw style
   reference, and do not fall back to image-to-video. For Seedance, write the
   prompt as an edit of the video, naming what stays. For example: "Edit
   @Video1: restyle every frame to match @Image1 (its palette, shading and
   line). Keep the camera movement, timing, poses and composition of @Video1
   unchanged." After a pilot, submit the remaining sections together once the
   user approves them.
6. **Inspect the take through the ending:** Seedance and similar models can animate a frozen subject, change
   the camera path or revert to the source look in the last second.

## When the result misses

Change the layer responsible for the miss. Wrong look: fix the anchor, not the
video prompt. Motion or composition drift: shorten or simplify the section, tell
the edit prompt what to keep, or try another video-conditioned endpoint. Style
fades over the clip: use a stronger edit mode, or a shorter section with its own
anchor.

# Make the picture support the story

Use this for explainers, factual shorts and shots whose meaning depends on a precise state.

Note what must stay fixed and which motion would contradict the story. A frozen animal breathing, a heartbeat during cardiac arrest, or particles passing through a closed valve can invalidate an otherwise beautiful shot.

Choose control to match the claim. Use authored geometry or deterministic 2D graphics for exact mechanisms, quantities and paths; generated imagery can establish atmosphere. Do not claim an illustration is a physical simulation.

For reference-led scenes, establish the composition before buying motion. Judge the returned movement, not the request wording.

Do not turn every episode into the same small diagram on an empty
background.

Inspect the actual source excerpt, not just its filename or metadata: a restrained
sleeping astronaut does not demonstrate free floating. Generated B-roll may create
atmosphere but must not masquerade as evidence of the event being explained. Mark
generated or reconstructed material as visualization when viewers could mistake it
for evidence.

## Real product UI is never generated

Software on screen whose text should read (an app, SaaS dashboard, website, UI
screenshots or recordings the user supplies) is built from those real screens:
compose them with motion and real type in
[make-product-demo](../make-product-demo/SKILL.md) or
[make-motion-graphics](../make-motion-graphics/SKILL.md), even when this skill was
loaded first or the type is AI-generated video. Never animate a UI screenshot with
image-to-video, reference-to-video or start/end frames, and never prompt a model to
render an interface: every video model garbles small text, and rewording the prompt
does not fix it. Generate only the shots without product UI (people, places, mood)
and cut them against the real screens. A generated shot that shows invented or

## Generate shots from references

A generated shot starts from its references, not a keyframe still. Each take (a
CONTINUE run of shots or panels in one place, within the model's duration, by
[multi-shot practice](#multi-shot-practice)) is one reference-to-video
generation: its characters from their approved Cast cards
(top-level `cast`), its location's reference image and any key prop's (the
user's, or made as [look development](references/film/look-dev.md#reference-images)
makes them, in the piece's look), with a prompt that writes the take from the
shot plan or storyboard. Default route: `minimax/h3-max/reference-to-video`, the
location and prop images in `reference_image_urls` (the adapter adds the Cast
images after them), the prompt in
[reference mode](references/models/minimax-h3.md#image-and-reference-modes)'s six
sections with `prompt_expansion_mode: "disabled"`, so the framing reaches the
model as written. Beyond 15 s or 9 images, use Seedance 2.5 `task: "reference"`
([its page](references/models/seedance.md)). A hand-drawn storyboard panel is a
waypoint in the prompt, never an image input.

A set image gives the place's design, not the shot's camera. MiniMax treats an
image named on its own as the frame to copy, and the cuts read as match cuts.

workshop environment in Image 1`) and the characters by name, give the shot's
size, angle and move in `detailed_description`, and leave the set image off a
close-up or insert where the set barely shows.

Keyframe stills come in when the user asks for them (stills, keyframes, start
and end frames, a frame-accurate storyboard) or brings an image to animate; then
follow [review stills before animating](#review-stills-before-animating).

## Wait, inspect, deliver

Video takes are long jobs. Once every take of the batch is submitted, end the turn with
one plain line: what is running, rough time left and credits committed so far. Voyager
resumes the conversation with an automatic notice listing each job's state and outputs;
then inspect and deliver as below without asking. Do not hold the turn open waiting or
write a polling loop. For a status question meanwhile, answer from one
`voyager jobs status JOB_ID --json`, then end the turn again.

Only a take expected to finish within a minute or two (a fast draft) is waited on in the
turn, with one bounded call over every `result.job.id` of the batch; on timeout, wait
again on the pending IDs only:

```sh
voyager jobs wait JOB_ID_1 JOB_ID_2 JOB_ID_3 --all --timeout 60 --json
```

`--timeout` is at most 120 seconds.
Check each job's `state`, not just `ok`; completed jobs list local paths in `outputs`.
A reused result, a collection failure, `provider_confirming` or `provider_lost`:
see [job states](references/cli.md#job-states).

Inspect the returned frame images, and run `media review` (add `--platform
shorts|tiktok|reels` for text under that platform's controls); act on each flag as
[export review](references/review.md) says, including its [AI-artifact pass](references/review.md#ai-artifact-pass)
(and its [one-take checks](references/review.md#one-take-checks) for a one-take),
trimming a flagged `checks.openingScale` take's `unstableFrames` from its head:

```sh
voyager media review PATH --json
ffmpeg -ss T -i FILE -frames:v 1 out.png
```

To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use
[hosted media understanding](../choose-media-model/references/understanding.md) (paid upload).

Generated motion drifts
most toward the end, so sample a generated take with
`--timestamps` about every second, as above for a 5 s take, ending about half a second
before the end of the duration `media review` reports, not the requested one, which
it can exceed; a timestamp at or past the end is refused. Read the frames, then
`voyager files present PATH --title "Clip" --deliverable "Teaser" --json`, with the
brief's deliverable name, the same for every draft and the final. Present each clip in the turn it finishes,
before you say it is ready: never report a clip done without presenting it.
Return an absolute local file link; never paste signed URLs or media bytes.
A single clip needs no assembly/re-encoding unless the requested edit requires it.
H3 Max can run about 0.7 s long: when the user asked for a length, trim to it.
The CLI inherits available harness identity and accepts `--workspace /path`; do not
invent Voyager session IDs or relocate previous outputs when changing workspaces.
